result.title: 改札の手前で
result.story:
美緒が二枚の切符を並べたのは、改札を通る直前だった。

「念のため、号車だけ合わせておこう」

そう言った亮の指が、切符の上で止まった。美緒の行き先は金沢、亮の行き先は長野だった。

背後から来た家族連れをよけ、二人は柱の脇へ移った。亮は自分の切符だけを持ち直した。

「金沢にしたんだ」

その言い方では、私が勝手に変えたみたいだ、と美緒は思った。

「した、というか。最初に行きたいって言ったよね」
「うん。でも、そのあと長野もいいねって」
「いいね、とは言ったけど」

美緒は携帯を取り出した。予約はそれぞれで、と決めた日のやり取りまで画面を戻す。亮も横からのぞき込んだが、肩が触れそうになると、わずかに身を引いた。

『じゃあ、そっちで。切符は各自取っておこう』

亮が送った文の一つ上には、美緒の『金沢の宿、まだ空いてるみたい』があった。けれど、その間に亮が送った長野の喫茶店の写真も挟まっていた。

「そっちって、金沢のことだとばかり思っていた」

美緒が言うと、亮は画面ではなく、発車案内を見上げた。

「僕は長野に行くつもりでいた。写真、気に入ったって言ってたから」

「それだけで……」と言いかけて、美緒は携帯を伏せた。自分もまた、宿の話に返事がなかったことを、賛成のしるしとして受け取っていた。

亮には、まだ釈然としないところがあった。美緒が金沢を望んでいたのなら、なぜ宿を取ったと言わなかったのか。そう尋ねようとして、宿のことをすっかり彼女任せにしていた自分に気づいた。

「宿は？」
「決めてから一緒に探そうと思って、まだ」
「そっか」

短い返事に安堵が混じったのがわかり、美緒は少しだけ腹が立った。無駄になった予約がなければ、それで済む行き違いでもない気がした。

発車案内の長野行きが点滅した。亮は時計を見てから、切符を二枚とも美緒の携帯の上に置いた。

「どっちが変更しやすいか、窓口で聞こうか」
「安いほうに合わせるってこと？」
「それもあるけど。……僕は、別々に行きたいわけじゃないから」

美緒は伏せていた携帯を裏返した。画面には、海に面した小さな宿の写真が残っていた。

「私、これを一緒に見たかったんだよね」

亮は今度は身を寄せ、写真を見た。

「うん。ちゃんと見てなかった」

美緒は切符を取り上げ、そのうち長野行きの一枚を亮に返した。

「喫茶店の写真、もう一回見せて。並んでる間に」

亮が携帯を探すのを待って、二人は変更窓口の列に加わった。どちらへ向かうかを決める前に、まだ見ておくものがあった。

To decide. 決めた is past tense; 決めて links actions; 決める is the plain form.
Day; here the day they agreed on the booking arrangement.
Exchange of messages or conversation.
As far as or back to; marks the point she scrolls back to.
Screen or the content displayed on it.
To move something back; here returning the screen to earlier messages.
The side; he looks at the phone from beside her.
To peer into or lean in to look closely at something.
Shoulder.
To touch or come into contact with something.
To be on the verge of doing something; their shoulders almost touch.
Slightly; by a very small amount.
To draw one's body back; here a small gesture of distancing.
Then; in that case.
That one or that option. Its unclear reference causes the destination mismatch.
Each person individually, taking responsibility for their own task.
To obtain or book tickets or accommodation. 取った is past tense; 取って links to a preparatory expression.
To send, here sending messages or a photo.
Written sentence or message.
One item or position; 一つ上 means one message above.
Accommodation or a place to stay.
Still or not yet, depending on context: still available, not yet booked, or something remaining to do.
To have availability, here rooms available at an accommodation. 空いてる is conversational for 空いている.
Apparently; seems to be the case based on available information.
To be present or exist. あった is past tense; なかった and なければ express absence.
However; introduces information that complicates the previous point.
The space or interval between things; here between messages.
Coffee shop or café.
Photograph.
To be inserted or situated between other things; the photo appeared between messages.
The thing or matter being referred to; turns a clause into something that can be discussed.
Had firmly assumed that; emphasizes a confident belief later shown to be mistaken.
Not A but something else; redirects attention from the screen to the departure display.
Departure information display at the station.
To look up at something.
I; Ryō's first-person pronoun.
To have an intention or an understanding of what one will do; the past form describes his continuing plan to go to Nagano.
To like something or find it appealing.
Because; gives the reason behind his assumption.
On that basis alone; expresses disbelief that such limited evidence was enough.
To start saying something but stop before finishing.
To turn something face down, here the phone.
Also; likewise, introducing her own similar assumption.
Talk or discussion; here the discussion about accommodation.
Reply or response.
Agreement or approval.
Sign or indication of something.
As; identifies how she interpreted the lack of a reply.
To interpret or take something in a particular way; she treated silence as agreement.
To remain unconvinced or feel that something does not quite make sense.
Aspect or point; something about the situation still troubles him.
To want or wish for something; here wanting Kanazawa as the destination.
If that was the case; frames a question based on her supposed wish.
Why.
Marks a question, here an unspoken question in his thoughts.
To ask. 尋ねよう is the volitional form, expressing an intended question.
To be about to or attempt to do something; he is about to ask a question.
Completely; entirely.
Leaving the matter entirely to her; 任せ attached to a person indicates reliance on that person to handle it.
To notice or realize something.
Together.
To look for something. 探そう expresses an intention or suggestion; 探す describes looking for the phone.
After doing something; establishes the order of deciding, searching, or acting.
Oh, I see; informal contraction of そうか.
Short or brief; describes the reply.
Relief after worry or uncertainty.
To be mixed into something; relief is detectable in his reply.
To understand or recognize; here recognizing his relief.
A little; to a small extent.
To feel angry or annoyed.
To be wasted or rendered useless; describes a potentially unusable booking.
For that to settle the matter or be sufficient; she feels avoiding a wasted booking would not resolve everything.
A mismatch in understanding or arrangements between people.
Not really or not merely that kind of thing; rejects treating the mismatch as easily resolved.
To have a feeling or impression; 気がした is past tense.
Bound for a destination; attached to a place name to identify the train or ticket.
To blink or flash, here on the departure display.
Clock or watch.
To look at or view. 見た and 見て are past and linking forms; 見たかった expresses a past wish; 見てなかった is conversational for 見ていなかった.
Both or all of a stated quantity; 二枚とも means both tickets.
To place or set something down.
Which of the two; conversational form of どちら.
Change or alteration, here changing a ticket's destination.
Easy to do; attached to a verb stem, here asking which ticket is easier to change.
Service counter or ticket desk.
To ask for information; 聞こうか suggests asking together.
Cheap or less expensive.
The option or side selected in a comparison; here the cheaper option.
Does that mean…?; conversational wording used to check the implication of a suggestion.
That is part of it, but…; acknowledges one reason before revealing another.
Separately; not together.
It is not that…; denies a particular intention or interpretation rather than simply stating the opposite.
To turn something over, here turning the phone face up.
Sea.
To face or overlook something; the accommodation faces the sea.
Small; a form used directly before a noun.
To remain; the photo was still displayed on the screen.
This; refers to the seaside accommodation shown in the photo.
Adds an explanatory, personal tone while inviting recognition of the speaker's feelings.
This time; contrasts his current gesture with his earlier withdrawal.
To move or lean closer; here a gesture of renewed closeness.
Properly or attentively; he admits he had not really looked at the photo.
To pick something up, here the tickets lying on the phone.
Of those; refers to one ticket among the two just mentioned.
To return or hand something back.
One more time; again.
To show something to someone; 見せて is an informal request.
To stand in line or queue. 並んでる is conversational for 並んでいる.
While or during; here while they are waiting in line.
To wait; here waiting for him to find his phone.
Counter that handles ticket changes.
Line or queue of people.
To join, here joining the queue.
Which of the two; more neutral than どっち.
To head toward a place or destination.
Before doing something; here before deciding their destination.
Things; here things they still need to look at, with an implied need to consider each other's wishes.
